state.misconception_label: Thinks alternate angles are always equal

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are arguing about alternate angles. Tom says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate. Katie says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are equal. Who is correct? ![Shows two non parallel lines that are intersected by another line. Angles P and Q are both on the outside of the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.](). I got Only
Katie because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Actually, in this case, angles \( p \) and \( q \) are not equal. They are alternate angles, which means they are on opposite sides of the transversal and are congruent. Let me show you a quick example to clarify this concept. Can you now explain to me what alternate angles are?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so I think alternate angles are the ones that are on opposite sides of the transversal, but I thought they were always equal. So, if they’re not equal when the lines aren’t parallel, does that mean they can be different? I'm a bit confused about when they actually are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Yes, you're on the right track! Alternate angles are indeed on opposite sides of the transversal, but they are not always equal, especially when the lines are not parallel. Let's focus on understanding why they are congruent in this case and how to distinguish them from other types of angles. Can you think of a scenario where alternate angles would be equal?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so I think alternate angles are equal when the lines are parallel, right? But if the lines aren’t parallel, then they can be different. I’m still a bit confused about how to tell when the lines are parallel just by looking at the angles. Can you help me with that?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher makes a critical error in Turn 1 by stating the angles ARE congruent when they're not (since lines aren't parallel), though the student does progress from thinking all alternate angles are equal to understanding they're only equal when lines are parallel.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher makes contradictory statements (claiming angles are both 'not equal' and 'congruent' simultaneously), fails to provide the promised worked example, and uses questioning rather than direct explanation, which deviates significantly from traditional direct instruction.
